name: connect-database-seed-restore
description: What: Put the Main Profisee database into a known, empty state: check the seed backup exists, stop the Profisee Windows service, restore the seed (connect/databases:BaseSeedBackupFileName) over the Main database, recycle every Main application pool, start the service, run Profisee Configuration on the restored seed (install-configure-upgrade), then set and prove the Main API key (connect-api-key-set-main). Why: A building block of the Connect pack; the bootstrap runs it first so the Main model is always built on a clean, empty database, whatever another pack left on the server. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; the bootstrap runs it. Running it alone replaces the Main Profisee database with the seed. Needs: the seed backup in the SQL Server default backup folder of connect/machines:DatabaseServerName: a configured, empty Profisee database of the same or an older version than the one under test, holding the API user; the install pack on this box; reference values: connect/databases:BaseSeedBackupFileName, connect/databases:MasterConnectionString, connect/databases:ProfiseeDatabaseName, connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerName, connect/machines:DatabaseServerName; no test running against this Profisee database. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check; when the seed check fails nothing was changed.

inline.description: What: Check the seed backup (connect/databases:BaseSeedBackupFileName) sits in the SQL Server default backup folder of the database server (connect/machines:DatabaseServerName), before anything is stopped or restored. Why: the restore below replaces the Main Profisee database; a missing seed must stop the run while the database is still untouched. Success: The seed backup is found. If it fails: copy the seed backup into the SQL Server default backup folder of the database server (the message names the folder), or correct connect/databases:BaseSeedBackupFileName; or check the database server is reachable from this box with Windows authentication.

What: On the application server, find the Windows service of this Profisee instance (connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, or the instance this workload targets): the service whose program lies in the installed Profisee folder that holds the instance's IIS application, never a typed name or a name prefix, because several instances and versions can share one server and the installer lets a person name the service anything. Only its short name is printed (nothing when the instance has none), into the run parameter InstanceServiceName that the service steps below read. Why: the service is stopped around a restore or a key change on releases that have one. Success: one name or nothing is printed; with nothing the service steps report Skipped, normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service. If it fails: the message says what was found: no IIS application for the instance (check the instance name in reference data), more than one service for the instance (names and programs listed: remove the stale one), or a service another instance in the same folder could own; or the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot reach the server over CredSSP.

What: Stop the Profisee Windows service on {{ApplicationServerName}} before IIS is stopped, recycled or restored under, so it holds no connection or cached state (skipped when this release has no Profisee Windows service). Why: Stop the Windows service so the next steps work on a quiet or a running Profisee instance, as they need. Success: The service on the target machine ends in the state the action asks for (Stop). If it fails: the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot manage services on that server over CredSSP, or the service did not reach the state in time (check it in services.msc there). Skipped when: the step Find The Instance Service found no Windows service for this instance, which is normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service.

What: Restore the seed backup (connect/databases:BaseSeedBackupFileName) over {{ProfiseeDatabaseName}} WITH REPLACE. The executor takes the database OFFLINE WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE first (disconnects the application server), and brings it back ONLINE if the restore fails. Why: the Main model is built on a clean, empty Profisee database, never on whatever another pack or an older run left there (entities outside the Connect family that use its domains stop the model build). Success: SQL Server finishes the restore of the database from the seed in its default backup folder. If it fails: Check the disk has room and the CrewChief account is sysadmin on the database server; the step before proved the file exists.

What: Recycle every application pool of {{ProfiseeInstanceName}} so no service keeps metadata or record caches from before the restore. The pools are found on the server at run time: the application pools that the IIS applications /<instance> and below use (whole path segments, so another instance whose name starts the same is never caught), never a typed list; recycle each of them. A built-in pool, or one that also serves something outside the instance, is never touched and is named in the output; the output lists every pool and what it serves. Why: Recycles or starts the IIS application pools so no service keeps caches from before a restore or a configuration change. Success: every pool found reaches Started. If it fails: the instance has no such IIS application on the server (check connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, or the instance this workload targets, against IIS Manager), no pool may be touched, a pool did not reach Started within 120 seconds, or the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot reach the server over CredSSP.

What: Start the Profisee Windows service on {{ApplicationServerName}} after IIS is back, so it reads the current database and key (skipped when this release has no Profisee Windows service). Why: Start the Windows service so the next steps work on a quiet or a running Profisee instance, as they need. Success: The service on the target machine ends in the state the action asks for (Start). If it fails: the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot manage services on that server over CredSSP, or the service did not reach the state in time (check it in services.msc there). Skipped when: the step Find The Instance Service found no Windows service for this instance, which is normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service.

What: Run Profisee Configuration on the restored seed (install pack building block install-configure-upgrade: upgrade, keeps the data). The seed may come from an older Profisee version, and only the database Configuration ran on last carries service sign-in ids this application server accepts; Configuration upgrades the seed to the version under test and writes new ids. A seed from a newer version than the installed Profisee cannot be used (Configuration only upgrades). Why: Runs the child workload 'install-configure-upgrade' so its tested steps are reused here, not repeated. Success: The child workload ends with every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Open the run output of 'install-configure-upgrade'; its first failed step says what to check.

What: Set the standard API key on the Main instance after the restore and Configuration (a clean Configuration issues a new key), restart IIS so every service reads it, and prove it through the gateway (pack rule: a workload that restores the Profisee database sets and verifies the key itself). Why: Runs the child workload 'connect-api-key-set-main' so its tested steps are reused here, not repeated. Success: The child workload ends with every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Open the run output of 'connect-api-key-set-main'; its first failed step says what to check.

steps.label: Set And Verify Main API Key

inputs.name: ProfiseeVersionNumber
inputs.description: Product version of the release under test (n.n.n): the Configuration program is found under it. Passed by the workload that runs this one (connect/environment:ProfiseeVersionNumber, or the lane's version).
